# Ship PA System
Every powered PA speaker anchored to a ship's grid joins that ship's public address network automatically - there's no wiring or configuration to do. Speakers carry the pilot's announcements and the ship's alarms to anyone standing near a working one.
## Placement
Any PA speaker anchored to the ship joins its network. A ship with no speakers at all announces through its air alarms instead, so most vessels are covered until a proper network goes in. A PA speaker goes together like an intercom: screw two steel sheets to a wall. Pry it back off with a crowbar to reclaim the steel.
## Situation codes
The pilot console's PA & Alarms panel sets a ship-wide situation code. Setting a code sounds its tone over every working speaker, shows a brief subtitle at the top of the screen for everyone on the grid, and posts it in chat.
- [color=#3fe05a]Code Green[/color] - normal operations. - [color=#ffd23f]Code Yellow[/color] - elevated readiness. - [color=#ff3030]Code Red[/color] - hostile action underway. - [color=#d0d0d0]Code Black[/color] - abandon ship.
## General quarters
The general quarters toggle sounds a looping klaxon on every speaker until it's secured again from the same panel. Alarms take priority over PA music; the music resumes at its current position when the alarm is secured. Walking between speakers does not restart the broadcast.
## Internet audio
Paste an HTTPS audio or video link into the PA panel and press Play. The link, any redirects, and the audio stream must all use HTTPS; plain HTTP streams are not supported. If something is already playing, the link joins the ship's queue (eight links at most) and plays when the track ends. Skip ends the current track, X takes a link out of the queue, Clear empties it, and Stop ends the track and empties the queue.
## Damage and repair
A speaker takes damage like any structure: light damage makes its audio muffle and cut out, heavy damage breaks it silent until repaired. Fix it with a welder, or with a ship repair tool once it's part of a ship's hull.
